text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- Austrians have spent as much as 5.4 billion schillings on petrol in neighbouring countries, lured by much cheaper prices across the border.
- Hospital doctors continue protests against Health Minister Christa Krammer's plans to introduce call duty only over weekends and holidays.
- Cooperation between Austria and NATO should be expanded, says Austrian Social Democrat Hannes Swoboda, a member of the European Parliament.
- Social Democrats and conservative People's Party have signed a new coalition agreement for Vienna's city government.
- High taxes and wage costs are a serious threat to Austrian industry's competitiveness in the European Union, research institute Wifo says.
- About 200 investors who have bought shares of textile maker Tiroler Loden in 1988 have sued Bank Austria, lead manager of the issue, claiming the bank issued incorrect figures in the prospectus.
- European Bank for Reconstruction and Development to take a 20 percent stake in Bank Austria Croatia.
- Foreign banks active in Austria are much more profitable then domestic banks, a study by research institute Wifo shows.
DIE PRESSE
- Retailers should not be allowed to raise prices for a period of several months after the introduction of the euro, Europe's planned single currency, Finance Minister Viktor Klima says.
- Snow falls across Austria wreak havoc on the country's roads.
- None of the indicative offers for the government's 70 percent voting stake in Creditanstalt have fulfilled all the criteria of the tender, the finance ministry said.
- Finance Minister Klima wants to reform Austria's tax system, raising inheritance taxes and introducing environmental incentives.
- U.S. officials are taking legal action against textile maker Linz Textil AG, accusing the company of price dumping.
- Privately-owned book store chain Libro may be bought for around one billion schillings by a consortium led by UnternehmensInvest (UIAG).
- Research institute WIFO expects further losses in Austria's ailing tourism industry.
KURIER
- Social Democrats and conservative People's Party fail to reach agreement on more flexible working hours.
- Austria to spend six billion schillings on new tanks, Defence Minister Werner Fasslabend says.
- Oberbank's pre-tax profits are expected to rise by more than 25 percent this year, reaching a new record level.
- Falling profits at Austria's largest bakery, Ankerbrot, may result in the loss of 200 jobs.
